Slice: Return Tool

Step 9 of 12 in Borrow and return a tool · after Tool Catalog — loan extended · before Tool Inventory — tool returned · State Change

Intent

Let a borrower bring a tool back and end their loan themselves, from My Loans. The tool is then back in the shed, for the next holder or for anyone to borrow. The return records whether it was late, which is what counts toward a neighbor being flagged.

Trigger & Actor

The borrower, from their own My Loans screen, for one of their own loans. My Loans offers Return on every loan it lists (INV-MYL-12), including overdue loans, loans whose tool was retired while out, and loans of a suspended neighbor. The shed manager does not record returns; a tool that never comes back is recorded lost instead (Record Tool Lost).

Command / Input

Command: Return Tool

A NeighborId or LoanId is a UUID.

FieldTypeRequiredRules / Validation
neighborIdNeighborIdyesThe neighbor returning, who must be the one making the request and the loan's borrower (INV-RET-1).
loanIdLoanIdyesThe loan to end. Must be a loan that has been checked out (INV-RET-11), and still out (INV-RET-2).

There is no field for the tool's condition: nothing about it is recorded on return. A damaged tool is the shed manager's to retire.

Trigger

Triggered by: screen My Loans @Neighbor

Event(s) Emitted

Event: Tool Returned → context Loans Read by: My Loans (the loan drops off), Tool Inventory and Tool Catalog (the tool is back in the shed), Holds To Fulfill (a returned tool with holds waiting), Overdue Loans To Notify and Undelivered Notices (the loan has ended), and Neighbors To Flag and Neighbors (whether the return was late, and the late return behind a flag).

FieldTypeImmutable Fact?Source / Notes
loanIdLoanIdyesFrom the command.
toolIdToolIdyesThe loan's tool, from its Tool Checked Out. Carried so views about tools and holds match on the tool directly.
toolNameTextyesSet by the system: the tool's name on the loan's Tool Checked Out.
neighborIdNeighborIdyesSet by the system: the borrower on the loan's Tool Checked Out (the same as the command's, by INV-RET-1). Carried so readers about neighbors match on the borrower directly.
dueDateDateyesSet by the system: the loan's due date in force at the moment of return (Tool Checked Out.dueDate, moved by any Loan Extended), the date late was judged against.
returnedAtInstantyesThe UTC moment the event is recorded, set by the system.
returnedOnDateyesSet by the system: the calendar date of returnedAt in the shed's local time zone.
lateBoolyesSet by the system: yes when returnedOn is after the loan's due date in force at the moment of return (INV-RET-4).

The event never changes. returnedOn and late are worked out once, by the command's handler, so every view reads the same answer.

Read Model / View

This slice produces no view of its own. Tool Returned ends the loan in My Loans, Overdue Loans To Notify and Undelivered Notices; puts the tool back in the shed on Tool Inventory and Tool Catalog (or drops a tool retired while out); adds a tool with holds waiting to Holds To Fulfill; and gives Neighbors To Flag and Neighbors a late or on-time return. Each is specified in its own doc, and all are eventually consistent.

Invariants / Business Rules

Once a loan is returned, no overdue notice goes out for it (INV-OLN-4, Overdue Loans To Notify). A returned tool with no holds waiting is available to borrow straight away; one with holds waiting is reserved, and until Hold Fulfilled is recorded only the neighbor at the front of the queue may check it out (INV-CHK-3a, Check Out Tool). Late returns count toward a neighbor being flagged, 3 within 90 days (Neighbors To Flag). Those rules are owned by those slices.

  • INV-RET-1: The borrower returns their own loan themselves, from My Loans.
    • The request must come from the neighbor it names, and the loan must be theirs. Sign-in, handled outside the model, supplies the acting neighbor's ID; a request whose neighbor ID isn't the signed-in neighbor's is refused requester-mismatch. The shed manager does not record returns.
  • INV-RET-2: Only a loan that is still out can be returned, and only once.
    • A loan ended by the shed manager recording the tool lost can't be returned.
    • A closed account never has a loan out, because an account can't be closed while tools are on loan (INV-CLS-7, Close Account).
  • INV-RET-3: Returning a tool records only Tool Returned.
    • Setting the tool aside for the first waiting hold is a separate system reaction to the return, recorded as Hold Fulfilled (Fulfill Hold).
  • INV-RET-4: A return is late when it happens after the loan's due date: from the start of the day after the due date, in the shed's local time.
    • A return on the due date itself is on time. The due date is the one in force at the moment of return: the latest Loan Extended's dueDate, or Tool Checked Out's if never extended.
    • Tool Returned records the answer as late, with the date of return as returnedOn.
  • INV-RET-5: An overdue loan can be returned.
  • INV-RET-7: A suspended neighbor can return a tool.
  • INV-RET-9: A tool retired while on loan can still be returned.
    • The return ends the loan as usual. The tool stays retired: it doesn't come back into the Tool Catalog or Tool Inventory, and no hold is waiting on it, because retiring it ended its holds.
  • INV-RET-10: Returning a loan that this borrower has already returned succeeds and records nothing.
    • So a double submit, or a retry after a lost response, never records a second return.
  • INV-RET-11: The loan must have been checked out.
  • INV-RET-12: A request with no sign-in is refused before anything else is checked.

Scenarios (Given / When / Then)

  • Happy path: on-time return, no holds (INV-RET-1, INV-RET-3, INV-RET-4)
    • Given: Ana (N1) has the cordless drill (T1) on loan L1, due 12 October, and no holds are waiting on it
    • When: at 15:00 on 11 October, shed time, Ana returns L1 from My Loans
    • Then: Tool Returned is recorded for L1, with toolId T1, the time it was recorded, returnedOn 11 October, and late no. Nothing else is recorded.
  • Return on the due date (INV-RET-4)
    • Given: L1 is due 12 October
    • When: Ana returns L1 at 23:59 on 12 October, shed time
    • Then: Tool Returned is recorded with returnedOn 12 October, late no.
  • Late return (INV-RET-4, INV-RET-5)
    • Given: L1 was due 12 October, and Overdue Notice Sent has been recorded for it
    • When: Ana returns L1 at 00:05 on 13 October, shed time
    • Then: Tool Returned is recorded with returnedOn 13 October, late yes.
  • Return after an extension (INV-RET-4)
    • Given: L1 was due 12 October, and Loan Extended moved its due date to 19 October
    • When: Ana returns L1 on 15 October
    • Then: Tool Returned is recorded with late no, judged against 19 October.
  • Return with a hold waiting (INV-RET-3)
    • Given: Ana has L1, and Ben's hold on T1 is at the front of the queue
    • When: Ana returns L1
    • Then: Tool Returned is recorded. No Hold Fulfilled is recorded by this command; setting T1 aside for Ben is Fulfill Hold's.
  • Suspended neighbor returns a tool (INV-RET-7)
    • Given: Ana is suspended and has L1 out
    • When: Ana returns L1 from My Loans
    • Then: Tool Returned is recorded for L1.
  • Returning a tool that was retired while on loan (INV-RET-9)
    • Given: Ana has the ladder (T2) on loan L2, and Tool Retired was recorded for T2 while it was out
    • When: Ana returns L2 from My Loans
    • Then: Tool Returned is recorded for L2, with toolId T2. T2 stays retired.
  • The same return twice (INV-RET-10)
    • Given: Tool Returned was recorded for L1
    • When: Ana's same Return Tool request for L1 arrives again
    • Then: the request succeeds and nothing new is recorded.
  • Loan already recorded lost (INV-RET-2)
    • Given: Tool Lost was recorded for Ana's loan L3
    • When: Ana asks to return L3
    • Then: refused with loan-ended: "This loan has ended." No event is recorded.
  • Someone else's loan (INV-RET-1)
    • Given: Ana has L1 out
    • When: Ben asks, for himself, to return L1
    • Then: refused with not-your-loan: "You can only return your own loans." No event is recorded.
  • A request in someone else's name (INV-RET-1)
    • Given: Ana has L1 out
    • When: a request from Ben asks to return L1 for Ana
    • Then: refused with requester-mismatch: "You can only return loans for yourself." No event is recorded.
  • Unknown loan (INV-RET-11)
    • Given: no loan has ID L9
    • When: Ana asks to return L9
    • Then: refused with loan-not-found: "There is no such loan." No event is recorded.
  • Not signed in (INV-RET-12)
    • Given: nobody is signed in
    • When: a request for returning a tool arrives
    • Then: refused with not-signed-in: "Please sign in." No event is recorded.

Alternate & Error Flows

Every refusal records nothing and returns one reason: the stable name, and the sentence shown to the borrower on the My Loans screen. The name is the contract; the sentence is the required wording of the message.

The checks run in this order, and the first that fails is the reason returned:

  1. not-signed-in (INV-RET-12): a request with no sign-in is refused first.
  2. requester-mismatch (INV-RET-1).
  3. loan-not-found (INV-RET-11).
  4. not-your-loan (INV-RET-1).
  5. If Tool Returned is already recorded for the loan, the request is a repeat: it succeeds and records nothing (INV-RET-10).
  6. loan-ended, if Tool Lost is recorded for the loan (INV-RET-2).
ReasonSentenceRule
not-signed-inPlease sign in.INV-RET-12
requester-mismatchYou can only return loans for yourself.INV-RET-1
loan-not-foundThere is no such loan.INV-RET-11
not-your-loanYou can only return your own loans.INV-RET-1
loan-endedThis loan has ended.INV-RET-2

requester-mismatch and loan-not-found can only come from a faulty or impersonating caller, not from the screen. A missing or malformed ID (not a UUID) is bad input, rejected before any rule is checked. It is not a refusal and has no reason name. The names mean the same conditions as in Extend Loan, and loan-ended uses the same sentence.

Suspension, an overdue loan and a retired tool never stop a return; there is no refusal for them.

Idempotency: a return is identified by its loan. A repeat after the loan was returned succeeds and records nothing. A loan ended by Tool Lost is refused, because returning it would be a different outcome from the one recorded.

Requests at the same moment: each Return Tool is decided against the loan's events as already recorded, one at a time per loan. Of a return and a Record Tool Lost for the same loan at once, whichever is decided first is recorded; the other finds the loan ended (a return then gets loan-ended, or succeeds as a repeat if the first was itself a return).

There are no external calls, retries or compensations in this slice.

Non-Functional Requirements

  • Security / authz: a borrower may return only their own loans (INV-RET-1); the shed manager doesn't record returns. Sign-in, handled outside the model, supplies the acting neighbor's ID; a request whose neighbor ID isn't the signed-in neighbor's is refused requester-mismatch.
  • PII & compliance: Tool Returned holds no name or email; it records which loan ended, when, and whether it was late.
  • Performance / SLA: none beyond the one-at-a-time rule above.

Dependencies & Read Models Affected

  • Upstream events this slice relies on, to apply its rules, and the fields it reads from each:
    • Tool Checked Out (Check Out Tool): loanId, toolId, neighborId, dueDate.
    • Loan Extended (Extend Loan): loanId, dueDate.
    • Tool Returned (this slice): loanId.
    • Tool Lost (Record Tool Lost): loanId.
    • These match slices/check-out-tool.md and slices/extend-loan.md. Record Tool Lost is specified in a slice not yet written in depth; it is checked against this key when it is.
  • Downstream read models / slices affected: My Loans, Tool Inventory, Tool Catalog, Holds To Fulfill, Overdue Loans To Notify, Undelivered Notices, Neighbors To Flag and Neighbors. Fulfill Hold reacts to a returned tool with holds waiting.

Open Questions

  • Flagged Neighbors and Suspended Neighbors were folded into the Neighbors view (model reshape 2026-11-01, merged-from on slices/neighbors.md v2): reword this doc's mentions of them to Neighbors — v2: reworded; Check Out Tool no longer feeds the merged Neighbors view, Return Tool does (2026-11-01)

State Changev2DraftDelta pending

Slice: Place Hold

Step 1 of 29 in Hold a tool for pickup · the story starts here · before My Holds · State Change

Intent

Let a neighbor get in line for a tool that isn't available to borrow right now, by placing a hold from the Tool Catalog. Holds on a tool are fulfilled in the order they were placed: when the tool is back in the shed, it is set aside for the neighbor at the front of the queue.

Trigger & Actor

A neighbor, from the Tool Catalog, on a tool that is checked out, set aside for a holder, or reserved (back in the shed with holds waiting, not yet set aside). The catalog is the same for every neighbor, so it offers Place Hold on every such tool to everyone; a neighbor who may not hold it is refused with a reason they can see. The shed manager doesn't place holds.

Command / Input

Command: Place Hold

A HoldId, ToolId or NeighborId is a UUID.

FieldTypeRequiredRules / Validation
holdIdHoldIdyesA UUID chosen by the caller for the new hold, so a retried request is recognised. Must not belong to a different hold already placed (INV-HOLD-13).
toolIdToolIdyesThe tool to hold. Must be a tool that has been added (INV-HOLD-14), not retired (INV-HOLD-3), and not available (INV-HOLD-2).
neighborIdNeighborIdyesThe neighbor placing the hold, who must be the one making the request (INV-HOLD-1). Must be a registered account (INV-HOLD-14), not closed (INV-HOLD-4) and not suspended (INV-HOLD-9).

Trigger

Triggered by: screen Tool Catalog @Neighbor

Event(s) Emitted

Event: Hold Placed → context Holds Read by: My Holds (its own slice, which shows the neighbor their place in the queue), Tool Catalog (holds waiting, and a tool's status), My Loans (a hold waiting on a borrowed tool), and Holds To Fulfill (the queue the hold fulfiller works from).

FieldTypeImmutable Fact?Source / Notes
holdIdHoldIdyesFrom the command. Identifies the hold everywhere from here on.
toolIdToolIdyesFrom the command.
toolNameTextyesSet by the system: the tool's name as recorded by Tool Added, copied so the hold's readers never look it up.
neighborIdNeighborIdyesFrom the command: the holder.
neighborNameTextyesSet by the system: the holder's name as recorded by Neighbor Registered.
neighborEmailTextyesSet by the system: the holder's email current when the hold is placed (Neighbor Registered, replaced by any Neighbor Email Changed).
placedAtInstantyesThe UTC moment the event is recorded, set by the system. For display only: the queue is the order Hold Placed is recorded, since two holds can share a timestamp.

Every field is fixed for good. A hold's later life (fulfilled, cancelled, expired, ended) is recorded by other events; nothing changes Hold Placed.

Read Model / View

This slice produces no view of its own. Hold Placed feeds four views, each specified in its own doc:

  • My Holds (slices/my-holds.md) shows the neighbor the new hold and its place in the queue.
  • Tool Catalog (slices/tool-catalog.md) counts it among the holds waiting on the tool.
  • My Loans (slices/my-loans.md) shows the borrower of the tool that someone is waiting.
  • Holds To Fulfill (slices/holds-to-fulfill.md) adds it to the tool's queue.

All are eventually consistent: the hold shows once each view has caught up with Hold Placed.

Invariants / Business Rules

A tool's state, for these rules, is tested against its events as already recorded, in this order; the first that holds wins:

  1. checked-out — a loan of the tool is open: Tool Checked Out recorded, and neither Tool Returned nor Tool Lost for that loan.
  2. set-aside — otherwise, a hold on the tool has been fulfilled and hasn't ended.
  3. reserved — otherwise, at least one hold on the tool is waiting.
  4. available — otherwise.

This is the same test the Tool Catalog uses for a tool's status.

A hold is waiting from Hold Placed until it is fulfilled or ends. A hold ends when it is cancelled or expires, when the holder checks the tool out, when the tool is retired or recorded lost, or when the holder closes their account. Once fulfilled, the tool is set aside for the holder until the end of the collect-by date, the set-aside date plus 3 days; a set-aside whose collect-by date has passed still counts as set aside until Hold Expired is recorded for it. Other slices record these endings; this slice reads them.

The Tool Catalog is the same for every neighbor, so it offers Place Hold on every tool that isn't available and can't hide the action from a neighbor who may not use it. Each rule below that refuses a neighbor (INV-HOLD-4, INV-HOLD-7, INV-HOLD-8, INV-HOLD-9) does so with a reason the neighbor can see.

  • INV-HOLD-1: A neighbor places a hold themselves, from the Tool Catalog, and only for themselves.
    • The neighbor ID must be the neighbor making the request. Sign-in, handled outside the model, supplies the acting neighbor's ID; a request whose neighbor ID isn't the signed-in neighbor's is refused requester-mismatch.
  • INV-HOLD-2: A hold can be placed on any tool that isn't available.
    • That is a tool that is checked out, set aside for a holder, or back in the shed with holds waiting but not yet set aside.
    • A hold on an available tool is refused. The neighbor checks it out instead.
  • INV-HOLD-3: A hold can't be placed on a retired tool.
    • A tool recorded lost is retired by that. Retiring a tool ends every hold on it.
  • INV-HOLD-4: A neighbor whose account is closed can't place a hold.
    • Closing an account ends all of that neighbor's holds.
  • INV-HOLD-5: A new hold joins the back of the tool's queue.
    • The order is the order Hold Placed events are recorded for the tool. placedAt is for display only, since two holds can share a timestamp. Holds on one tool are decided one at a time, so no two share a place.
    • Holds are fulfilled in queue order; that is Fulfill Hold's rule (INV-FUL-2).
  • INV-HOLD-7: A neighbor can have only one hold on a given tool.
    • A second hold by the same neighbor on the same tool is refused, whether their first hold is waiting or set aside.
    • A hold that has ended doesn't count. After cancelling, or once their hold has expired, the neighbor may hold the tool again, at the back of the queue.
  • INV-HOLD-8: A neighbor can't place a hold on a tool they have on loan themselves.
  • INV-HOLD-9: A suspended neighbor can't place a new hold.
    • Holds they placed before the suspension keep their place in the queue.
  • INV-HOLD-10: A neighbor with an overdue loan may place a hold.
    • The overdue loan stops them collecting the tool if it is set aside for them (Check Out Tool, INV-CHK-5), not placing the hold.
  • INV-HOLD-11: There is no limit on how many holds one neighbor can have at once.
  • INV-HOLD-13: Placing a hold with a hold ID that is already used places no new hold.
    • A repeat with the same tool and neighbor succeeds and records nothing new, whatever has happened to the hold since. A repeat with a different tool or neighbor is refused (hold-id-in-use).
  • INV-HOLD-14: The tool must have been added, and the neighbor must be a registered account.
  • INV-HOLD-15: A request with no sign-in is refused before anything else is checked.

Scenarios (Given / When / Then)

  • Happy path: first hold on a checked-out tool (INV-HOLD-2, INV-HOLD-5)
    • Given: Ana (N1) has the cordless drill (T1) on loan, due 12 October, and no holds are waiting on it. Ben (N2) is active.
    • When: Ben places hold H1 on T1 from the Tool Catalog
    • Then: Hold Placed is recorded for H1: T1, N2, and the time it was placed.
  • Second hold queues behind the first (INV-HOLD-5)
    • Given: T1 is checked out, and Ben's hold H1 on it is waiting
    • When: Cleo (N3) places hold H2 on T1
    • Then: Hold Placed is recorded for H2, after H1. H2 is behind H1 in T1's queue.
  • Hold on a set-aside tool (INV-HOLD-2)
    • Given: T1 was returned and is set aside for Ben's hold H1, and no other hold is waiting
    • When: Cleo places hold H2 on T1
    • Then: Hold Placed is recorded for H2, behind Ben's set-aside.
  • Hold on a reserved tool (INV-HOLD-2)
    • Given: T1 has just been returned, Ben's hold H1 is waiting, and Hold Fulfilled has not yet been recorded
    • When: Cleo places hold H2 on T1
    • Then: Hold Placed is recorded for H2, behind H1.
  • Available tool (INV-HOLD-2)
    • Given: the ladder (T2) is in the shed with no holds
    • When: Ben tries to place a hold on T2
    • Then: refused with tool-available: "This tool is available. Check it out instead." No event is recorded.
  • Retired tool (INV-HOLD-3)
    • Given: T1 was retired while Ana had it on loan
    • When: Ben tries to place a hold on T1
    • Then: refused with tool-retired: "This tool has been retired." No event is recorded.
  • Already holding this tool (INV-HOLD-7)
    • Given: T1 is checked out, and Ben's hold H1 on it is waiting
    • When: Ben tries to place hold H3 on T1
    • Then: refused with already-holding: "You already have a hold on this tool." No event is recorded.
  • Already holding this tool, set aside for them (INV-HOLD-7)
    • Given: T1 is set aside for Ben's hold H1
    • When: Ben tries to place hold H3 on T1
    • Then: refused with already-holding: "You already have a hold on this tool." No event is recorded.
  • Holding again after cancelling (INV-HOLD-7)
    • Given: T1 is checked out, Ben's hold H1 on it was cancelled, and Cleo's hold H2 is waiting
    • When: Ben places hold H4 on T1
    • Then: Hold Placed is recorded for H4, behind H2.
  • Holding again after expiry (INV-HOLD-7)
    • Given: T1 was set aside for Ben's hold H1, Hold Expired was recorded for H1, and Cleo now has T1 on loan
    • When: Ben places hold H5 on T1
    • Then: Hold Placed is recorded for H5.
  • Tool on loan to the neighbor (INV-HOLD-8)
    • Given: Ana has T1 on loan
    • When: Ana tries to place a hold on T1
    • Then: refused with tool-on-loan-to-you: "You have this tool on loan." No event is recorded.
  • Suspended neighbor (INV-HOLD-9)
    • Given: T1 is checked out by Ana, and Ben is suspended
    • When: Ben tries to place a hold on T1
    • Then: refused with neighbor-suspended: "You can't place holds while your account is suspended." No event is recorded.
  • Closed account (INV-HOLD-4)
    • Given: T1 is checked out by Ana, and Ben's account is closed
    • When: a hold on T1 is requested for Ben
    • Then: refused with account-closed: "This account is closed." No event is recorded.
  • Neighbor with an overdue loan (INV-HOLD-10)
    • Given: Ben has the ladder on loan, overdue, and Ana has T1 on loan
    • When: Ben places hold H6 on T1
    • Then: Hold Placed is recorded for H6.
  • Holds on several tools (INV-HOLD-11)
    • Given: Ben's hold H1 on T1 is waiting, and the hedge trimmer (T3) is checked out by Ana
    • When: Ben places hold H7 on T3
    • Then: Hold Placed is recorded for H7. Ben now has holds on T1 and T3.
  • A hold for someone else (INV-HOLD-1)
    • Given: T1 is checked out by Ana
    • When: a request from Ben asks to place a hold on T1 for Cleo
    • Then: refused with requester-mismatch: "You can only place holds for yourself." No event is recorded.
  • Unknown tool (INV-HOLD-14)
    • Given: no tool has ID T9
    • When: Ben asks to place a hold on T9
    • Then: refused with tool-not-found: "There is no such tool." No event is recorded.
  • Unknown neighbor (INV-HOLD-14)
    • Given: T1 is checked out by Ana, and no account has neighbor ID N9
    • When: a hold on T1 is requested for N9
    • Then: refused with neighbor-not-found: "There is no such neighbor." No event is recorded.
  • Hold on a lapsed set-aside (INV-HOLD-2)
    • Given: T1 was set aside for Ben's hold H1, collect by 17 October, and Hold Expired hasn't been recorded for H1
    • When: on 18 October, Cleo places hold H8 on T1
    • Then: Hold Placed is recorded for H8. T1 still counts as set aside, not available.
  • Lapsed holder holds again before expiry (INV-HOLD-7)
    • Given: T1 was set aside for Ben's hold H1, collect by 17 October, and Hold Expired hasn't been recorded for H1
    • When: on 18 October, Ben tries to place hold H9 on T1
    • Then: refused with already-holding: "You already have a hold on this tool." No event is recorded. Once Hold Expired is recorded for H1, he may hold T1 again.
  • The same request arrives twice (INV-HOLD-13)
    • Given: Hold Placed was recorded for H1: T1, Ben
    • When: the same Place Hold request for H1, T1, Ben arrives again
    • Then: the request succeeds and nothing new is recorded. Ben still has one hold on T1.
  • The same request after the hold ended (INV-HOLD-13)
    • Given: Hold Placed was recorded for H1: T1, Ben, and H1 has since been cancelled
    • When: the same Place Hold request for H1 arrives again
    • Then: the request succeeds and nothing new is recorded. H1 stays cancelled.
  • A hold ID reused for a different hold (INV-HOLD-13)
    • Given: Hold Placed was recorded for H1: T1, Ben
    • When: a Place Hold request arrives for H1 with T3, Ben
    • Then: refused with hold-id-in-use: "That hold ID is already used by another hold." No event is recorded.
  • Not signed in (INV-HOLD-15)
    • Given: nobody is signed in
    • When: a request for placing a hold arrives
    • Then: refused with not-signed-in: "Please sign in." No event is recorded.

Alternate & Error Flows

Every refusal records nothing and returns one reason: the stable name, and the sentence shown to the neighbor on the Tool Catalog screen. The name is the contract; the sentence is the required wording of the message.

The checks run in this order, and the first that fails is the reason returned:

  1. not-signed-in (INV-HOLD-15): a request with no sign-in is refused first.
  2. requester-mismatch (INV-HOLD-1): who is asking is settled next, before any other rule.
  3. The hold ID is already used (INV-HOLD-13): a repeat with the same details succeeds with nothing recorded; otherwise hold-id-in-use.
  4. tool-not-found, then neighbor-not-found (INV-HOLD-14).
  5. tool-retired (INV-HOLD-3).
  6. account-closed, then neighbor-suspended (INV-HOLD-4, INV-HOLD-9).
  7. tool-on-loan-to-you (INV-HOLD-8).
  8. already-holding (INV-HOLD-7).
  9. tool-available (INV-HOLD-2).
ReasonSentenceRule
not-signed-inPlease sign in.INV-HOLD-15
hold-id-in-useThat hold ID is already used by another hold.INV-HOLD-13
requester-mismatchYou can only place holds for yourself.INV-HOLD-1
tool-not-foundThere is no such tool.INV-HOLD-14
neighbor-not-foundThere is no such neighbor.INV-HOLD-14
tool-retiredThis tool has been retired.INV-HOLD-3
account-closedThis account is closed.INV-HOLD-4
neighbor-suspendedYou can't place holds while your account is suspended.INV-HOLD-9
tool-on-loan-to-youYou have this tool on loan.INV-HOLD-8
already-holdingYou already have a hold on this tool.INV-HOLD-7
tool-availableThis tool is available. Check it out instead.INV-HOLD-2

hold-id-in-use, tool-not-found and neighbor-not-found can only come from a faulty caller, not from the screen. A missing or malformed ID (not a UUID) is bad input, rejected before any rule is checked. It is not a refusal and has no reason name. The names and sentences shared with Check Out Tool (tool-not-found, neighbor-not-found, tool-retired, account-closed) are worded the same there.

Idempotency: a repeated request with the same hold ID, tool and neighbor succeeds and records nothing new, even if the hold has since been fulfilled, cancelled, expired or ended. So a retry after a lost response never places a second hold.

Requests at the same moment: each Place Hold is decided against the tool's holds and loans as already recorded, one at a time per tool. Two neighbors holding the same tool together are both recorded, in the order they are decided. The same neighbor sending two holds on one tool together gets one recorded; the other is refused with already-holding.

A set-aside past its collect-by date still counts as set aside until Hold Expired is recorded for it. Until then the tool is not available, so a hold on it is accepted (INV-HOLD-2), and the lapsed holder's own hold still counts as theirs (INV-HOLD-7).

There are no external calls, retries or compensations in this slice. Placing a hold sends no email.

Non-Functional Requirements

  • Security / authz: a neighbor may place a hold only for themselves (INV-HOLD-1); the shed manager doesn't place holds. Sign-in, handled outside the model, supplies the acting neighbor's ID; a request whose neighbor ID isn't the signed-in neighbor's is refused requester-mismatch.
  • PII & compliance: Hold Placed links a neighbor to a tool. It holds no name or email; those stay on Neighbor Registered and Neighbor Email Changed.
  • Performance / SLA: none beyond the one-at-a-time rule above.

Dependencies & Read Models Affected

  • Upstream events this slice relies on, to apply its rules, and the fields it reads from each:
    • Tool Added (Add Tool): toolId.
    • Tool Retired (Retire Tool): toolId.
    • Tool Lost (Record Tool Lost): loanId.
    • Tool Checked Out (Check Out Tool): loanId, toolId, neighborId.
    • Tool Returned (Return Tool): loanId.
    • Hold Placed (this slice): holdId, toolId, neighborId.
    • Hold Fulfilled (Fulfill Hold): holdId.
    • Hold Cancelled (Cancel Hold): holdId.
    • Hold Expired (Expire Hold): holdId.
    • Neighbor Registered (Register Neighbor): neighborId.
    • Neighbor Suspended (Suspend Neighbor): neighborId.
    • Neighbor Reinstated (Reinstate Neighbor): neighborId.
    • Neighbor Account Closed (Close Account): neighborId.
    • These keys match slices/add-tool.md, slices/register-neighbor.md, slices/check-out-tool.md, slices/tool-inventory.md and slices/tool-catalog.md. The others are specified in slices not yet written in depth; each is checked against these keys when it is.
  • Downstream read models / slices affected: My Holds, Tool Catalog, My Loans and Holds To Fulfill (the new hold). Fulfill Hold sets the tool aside for the front of the queue; Cancel Hold, Expire Hold, Check Out Tool, Retire Tool, Record Tool Lost and Close Account end holds; Extend Loan refuses while a hold is waiting.

Open Questions

None.

State Viewv2DraftDelta pending

Slice: Holds To Fulfill

Step 14 of 29 in Hold a tool for pickup · after Undelivered Notices — hold cancelled · before Fulfill Hold · State View

Intent

The hold fulfiller's to-do list: every tool that is back in the shed, not set aside for anyone, with a hold waiting, and which hold is next in line for it. The hold fulfiller works through it, so a returned tool is set aside for the neighbor at the front of its queue.

Trigger & Actor

  • Actor: the Hold Fulfiller, a system reaction in the Fulfill Hold slice. No person reads this list, and it has no screen.
  • What the fulfiller does with it: for each tool on the list, it issues Fulfill Hold for the front hold, which records Hold Fulfilled (Fulfill Hold slice).

Read Model / View

  • View: Holds To Fulfill built from events: "Hold Placed", "Hold Collected", "Tool Returned", "Hold Cancelled", "Tool Checked Out", "Hold Fulfilled", "Hold Expired"
  • Consumed by: the Hold Fulfiller (Fulfill Hold). Internal: no ui.
  • Freshness / consistency expectation: eventual. A tool joins or leaves the list shortly after the event that causes it is recorded (seconds, not minutes). Fulfill Hold checks its own rules when it runs, so acting on a row a moment out of date sets nothing aside wrongly.

One row per tool on the list. ToolId, HoldId and NeighborId are UUIDs.

FieldTypeSource / Notes
toolIdToolIdHold Placed.toolId.
holdIdHoldIdDerived: the front hold: the first hold on toolId, in the order Hold Placed was recorded, that is still waiting (INV-HTF-2).
neighborIdNeighborIdDerived: the front hold's holder, from its Hold Placed.

Bookkeeping. For every tool that has holds, the view keeps: whether a loan of it is open (from Tool Checked Out until Tool Returned or Tool Lost for that loan); whether a hold on it is set aside (from Hold Fulfilled until that hold ends); and its waiting holds, with holder, in the order Hold Placed was recorded. None of this is returned except the row.

Waiting and ending. A hold is waiting from Hold Placed until it is fulfilled or ends. A hold ends when Hold Cancelled, Hold Expired or Hold Collected is recorded for it. Retiring the tool, recording it lost and closing the holder's account each end holds by recording Hold Cancelled for them (Retire Tool, Record Tool Lost, Close Account). This list hears only the Holds events for holds.

Queries

  • List tools to fulfill. Takes nothing. Returns every row: toolId, and the front hold's holdId and neighborId. There is no paging. The order doesn't matter to the fulfiller, which acts on each tool separately.

Invariants / Business Rules

The list has no screen; only the hold fulfiller reads it. The front holder is never passed over, even when they are suspended or have an overdue loan and can't collect: the tool is set aside for them, and if they don't collect it by the end of the collect-by date the hold expires (Fulfill Hold, INV-FUL-8; Expire Hold). This view doesn't hear suspension or loans of other tools, so it never skips anyone.

  • INV-HTF-1: A tool is on the list exactly when all of these hold, tested against its current facts: no loan of it is open, no hold on it is set aside, and at least one hold on it is waiting.
    • A loan is open from Tool Checked Out until Tool Returned or Tool Lost for that loan. A hold is set aside from Hold Fulfilled until it ends; a set-aside whose collect-by date has passed still counts until Hold Expired is recorded for it.
    • The test reads current facts, not the order events arrived in. So a tool on loan is never on the list, however many holds wait on it, and whatever ended its last set-aside.
  • INV-HTF-2: Each item names the hold at the front of the tool's queue: the earliest-placed hold still waiting.
    • "Earliest-placed" is the order Hold Placed was recorded for the tool, not placedAt, since two holds can share a timestamp.
  • INV-HTF-3: When one of its holds is fulfilled, the tool leaves the list: the hold is now set aside (INV-HTF-1).
  • INV-HTF-4: When a set-aside ends without the holder collecting it (the hold expires or is cancelled, including by the holder closing their account), the tool joins the list if INV-HTF-1 then holds: no loan open and another hold waiting.
    • With no hold waiting, the tool becomes available and stays off the list. If someone checked it out after the collect-by date and before Hold Expired, it stays off the list until that loan ends.
  • INV-HTF-5: When the holder at the front of the queue checks the tool out before their hold is fulfilled, the tool leaves the list: a loan is now open, and that checkout ended their hold.
    • The next hold waits for the tool's return.
  • INV-HTF-6: When a waiting hold ends, the next waiting hold becomes the front. If no hold is left waiting, the tool leaves the list (INV-HTF-1).
  • INV-HTF-7: Retiring a tool, or recording it lost, ends all its holds: Retire Tool and Record Tool Lost record Hold Cancelled for each. With no hold left waiting, the tool leaves the list, or never joins it.
    • A tool is recorded lost only while it is on loan, so it is never on the list at that moment. Its holds are cancelled, and it never comes onto the list.
    • A tool retired while on loan never joins the list when it is returned: its holds were cancelled with it.
  • INV-HTF-9: Applying the same event twice leaves the list as if it had been applied once.

Scenarios (Given / When / Then)

  • Returned with a hold waiting (INV-HTF-1, INV-HTF-2)
    • Given: Ana has the cordless drill (T1) on loan L1, and Ben's hold H1 on it was placed before Cleo's hold H2
    • When: Tool Returned is recorded for L1, tool T1
    • Then: T1 is on the list, with front hold H1, Ben.
  • Returned with no hold waiting (INV-HTF-1)
    • Given: Ana has T1 on loan L1, with no holds on it
    • When: Tool Returned is recorded for L1
    • Then: T1 is not on the list.
  • Hold placed on a tool on loan (INV-HTF-1)
    • Given: Ana has T1 on loan
    • When: Hold Placed is recorded for Ben's hold H1 on T1
    • Then: T1 is not on the list.
  • Holds placed in the same instant (INV-HTF-2)
    • Given: Ana has T1 on loan
    • When: Hold Placed is recorded for H1 (Ben) and then H2 (Cleo), both with the same placedAt, and Tool Returned is then recorded for Ana's loan
    • Then: T1 is on the list with front hold H1: the order recorded decides.
  • Hold fulfilled (INV-HTF-3)
    • Given: T1 is on the list, with front hold H1 and H2 behind it
    • When: Hold Fulfilled is recorded for H1
    • Then: T1 leaves the list.
  • Set-aside expires, another hold waiting (INV-HTF-4)
    • Given: T1 is set aside for H1, and H2 is waiting
    • When: Hold Expired is recorded for H1
    • Then: T1 is back on the list, with front hold H2.
  • Set-aside expires, no hold waiting (INV-HTF-4)
    • Given: T1 is set aside for H1, and no other hold is waiting
    • When: Hold Expired is recorded for H1
    • Then: T1 is not on the list.
  • Set-aside past its collect-by date, not yet expired (INV-HTF-1)
    • Given: T1 is set aside for H1, collect by 17 October, and H2 is waiting
    • When: the list is read on 18 October, before Hold Expired is recorded for H1
    • Then: T1 is not on the list. It joins, with front hold H2, once Hold Expired lands.
  • Lapsed set-aside, next holder collects before expiry (INV-HTF-1, INV-HTF-4)
    • Given: T1 was set aside for Ben's H1, his collect-by date has passed, Cleo's H2 and Dan's H3 are waiting, and Cleo checked T1 out (ending H2) before Hold Expired was recorded for H1
    • When: Hold Expired is recorded for H1
    • Then: T1 is not on the list: Cleo's loan is open. When Tool Returned is recorded for Cleo's loan, T1 joins the list with front hold H3.
  • Set-aside cancelled, another hold waiting (INV-HTF-4)
    • Given: T1 is set aside for H1, and H2 is waiting
    • When: Hold Cancelled is recorded for H1
    • Then: T1 is back on the list, with front hold H2.
  • Set-aside holder closes their account (INV-HTF-4)
    • Given: T1 is set aside for Ben's H1, and Cleo's H2 is waiting
    • When: Close Account records Hold Cancelled for H1, because Ben closed his account
    • Then: T1 is back on the list, with front hold H2.
  • Front hold cancelled before it is fulfilled (INV-HTF-6)
    • Given: T1 is on the list, with front hold H1 and H2 behind it
    • When: Hold Cancelled is recorded for H1
    • Then: T1 stays on the list, with front hold H2.
  • Last waiting hold cancelled (INV-HTF-6)
    • Given: T1 is on the list, with front hold H1 and no other hold
    • When: Hold Cancelled is recorded for H1
    • Then: T1 leaves the list.
  • Front holder collects before the hold is fulfilled (INV-HTF-5)
    • Given: T1 is on the list, with front hold H1 (Ben) and H2 behind it
    • When: Tool Checked Out is recorded for T1 and Ben, with Hold Collected for H1
    • Then: T1 leaves the list (the loan is open, and H1 is gone from the queue). H2 waits for T1's next return.
  • Tool retired (INV-HTF-7)
    • Given: T1 is on the list, with front hold H1
    • When: Retire Tool records Hold Cancelled for H1, with Tool Retired for T1
    • Then: T1 leaves the list.
  • Retired while on loan, then returned (INV-HTF-7)
    • Given: Ana has T1 on loan with H1 waiting, and the shed manager retired T1, which recorded Hold Cancelled for H1
    • When: Tool Returned is recorded for Ana's loan
    • Then: T1 is not on the list.
  • Tool recorded lost while holds wait (INV-HTF-7)
    • Given: Ana has T1 on loan L1, and H1 is waiting on it
    • When: Record Tool Lost records Hold Cancelled for H1, with Tool Lost for L1
    • Then: H1 is gone, and T1 never joins the list.
  • Same event applied twice (INV-HTF-9)
    • Given: T1 is on the list once, with front hold H1
    • When: the same Tool Returned is applied again
    • Then: T1 is still on the list once, with front hold H1.

Alternate & Error Flows

  • Repeated events: every event is applied idempotently (INV-HTF-9). An event applied a second time leaves the list as it was after the first.
  • Events for a hold that has ended: a later Hold Cancelled, Hold Expired or Hold Fulfilled for a hold that has already ended (a replay) changes nothing.
  • The fulfiller reads a tool twice before Hold Fulfilled lands: the list may return the same tool on two reads in a row. Fulfilling a hold only once, and only while the tool is still free, is Fulfill Hold's rule (INV-FUL-3), enforced when it records Hold Fulfilled; this list raises no errors of its own.

Non-Functional Requirements

  • Security / authz: read only by the Hold Fulfiller. No person or screen reads it.
  • PII & compliance: holds neighbor IDs only, no names or emails.
  • Performance / SLA: none beyond the freshness above. How soon after a return the tool is set aside is Fulfill Hold's concern.

Dependencies & Read Models Affected

  • Upstream events this slice relies on, and the fields it reads from each:
    • Hold Placed (Place Hold): holdId, toolId, neighborId.
    • Hold Cancelled (Cancel Hold): holdId.
    • Hold Fulfilled (Fulfill Hold): holdId, toolId.
    • Hold Expired (Expire Hold): holdId.
    • Tool Checked Out (Check Out Tool): loanId, toolId (a loan is open).
    • Hold Collected (Collect Hold): holdId (the hold leaves the queue).
    • Tool Returned (Return Tool): loanId, toolId.
    • Hold Cancelled is also recorded by Retire Tool, Record Tool Lost and Close Account, one per hold they end.
    • These match slices/place-hold.md, slices/check-out-tool.md and slices/return-tool.md, and Hold Fulfilled as Fulfill Hold is being written. The others are specified in slices not yet written in depth; each is checked against these keys when it is.
  • Downstream read models / slices affected: Fulfill Hold, whose fulfiller works from this list and records Hold Fulfilled.

Open Questions

None.
